subject: Private cluster landing: tiered node roles, PV lifecycle and egress governance
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@stellarnet.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Park <rachel.park@stellarnet.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private cluster intake: requirements and constraints

Hi Marissa / Rachel,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We've pulled together a high-level requirements spreadsheet (attached) and would like Redwood's advice on an on-prem landing for our inference workloads. Key constraints:

- Air-gapped site in our AZ-3 datacenter (no outbound internet except through an approved egress proxy).
- 20 inference GPUs initially (mix of A5000 and A8000), burstable to 40 for seasonal workloads.
- Persistent model store must be encrypted-at-rest and replicable across two racks.
- We need a policy for zero-trust egress (only to our monitoring/proxy endpoints).
- SOC2 and ISO audit expectations; will need KMS/HSM integration for keys.

High-level asks: recommended node roles (control vs infra vs inference), PV strategy for model artifacts and checkpoints, snapshot/retention guidance, and any obvious blockers for our air-gap egress requirements.

Can you propose a short mutual action plan and a time for a technical review next week?

Thanks,
Evan
Lead Platform Engineer
StellarNet

Hi Evan — thanks for the brief and the attachment. This is a good starting point.

We can absolutely support an air-gapped/private deployment with rack-level replication and KMS-backed keys. To make our technical review efficient, can you confirm / provide the following before the call:

1) Expected sustained QPS (tokens/sec) and model memory footprints for the 20 GPU baseline (so we can size NVMe/host RAM vs blockstore).
2) Are the GPUs colocated on dedicated compute nodes or shared with customer services?
3) Do you have a site-approved egress proxy hostname/IP and a list of outbound destinations for image pulls (if needed)?
4) KMS details: vendor (HashiCorp Vault / AWS CloudHSM / Vormetric) and whether you can provide a staging key for validation.

Proposed mutual action plan (30–45 minute tech review):
- Discovery: confirm workloads, SNAT/egress constraints, and KMS.
- Topology proposal: control plane HA, node-class mapping (inference / infra / storage), PG/blockstore options.
- PV lifecycle: checkpoint cadence, hot/warm tiering, archival strategy (on-prem object or removable media).
- Risk/next steps: identify any audit or air-gap blockers and scope pilot.

I'll loop in our deployment lead (PrIyom) and infrastructure architect (Irene) to join the call. How does Wed 3/18 10:00am PT look?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Private cluster intake: requirements and constraints — prep for Wed

Team — forwarding StellarNet intake. Wed 3/18 10am PT set for the review. Evan is the lead platform engineer; Rachel will own procurement/ops.

Goal for our prep: come in with a concrete node-class and storage-profile recommendation that we can walk them through in 20 minutes. Key constraints called out: air-gap / egress proxy, rack replication, KMS/HSM.

Suggested agenda items we should cover (short bullets):
- Control plane: 3x control VMs ± keepalived for VIP, etcd replication strategy (local raft across racks) — confirm whether they prefer an external etcd appliance.
- Node classes:
  * inference-nodes: GPU-only, ephemeral NVMe for KV/cache, top-of-rack L2 peer for model warmups.
  * infra-nodes: small CPU footprint, run CSI controllers, logging/metrics aggregator.
  * storage-nodes: blockstore (replicated LVM/ceph OSDs) for model store with encryption at rest.
- PV lifecycle: immutable model artifacts (store in blockstore + periodic snapshots to on-prem object store), checkpoint dirs on host for streaming writes, retention policies (30d hot, 90d warm, archive to object).
- Egress: strict egress to their proxy; we need a whitelist and potential outbound allowlist for image pre-seeding.

Action items before call:
- PrIyom: quick node-sizing sketch per GPU type + sample PV IOPS per model size.
- Irene: any air-gap deployment notes (image bootstrapping options, repo mirroring) and KMS integration checklist.

I'll run the call and handle meeting notes.

—Marissa
From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private cluster intake: requirements and constraints — prep for Wed

Thanks — quick recommendations below we can present as a starting point. Kept it conservative given air-gap and SOC2 needs.

1) Control plane
- 3x control VMs (odd quorum) across two racks with proxy VIP via keepalived. Use local etcd raft (3 members) — avoids external dependency.
- Control VMs: 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM / 200GB boot + 1x NVMe for etcd WAL (separate device for durability).

2) Node-class mapping and counts (baseline 20 GPUs):
- inference-large (A8000) — 8 nodes x 1 GPU each OR 4 nodes x 2 GPUs, prefer 1 GPU-per-node for isolation (recommend 8 x 1 for A8000).
- inference-medium (A5000) — 6 nodes x 2 GPUs (12 GPUs total).
- infra-nodes — 2 nodes (controllers, CSI, logging, metrics, sidecars)
- storage-nodes — 3 nodes running blockstore/replication (Ceph OSDs or mirrored LVM + backup target)

3) Storage profiles
- Hot (ephemeral NVMe): model warming, KV cache — local NVMe on inference nodes (fast, non-replicated).
- Persistent (blockstore, encrypted): model artifacts and checkpoints — replicated across storage-nodes with synchronous replication within rack and async cross-rack replication for recovery.
- Archive: on-prem S3-compatible object store (MinIO/Ceph RGW) with lifecycle policy to removable media for long-term retention.

4) PV lifecycle and retention
- Checkpoint cadence: configurable; default keep last 3 checkpoints on blockstore, daily archival snapshot to object store.
- Snapshots: use block-level snapshots for fast rollback; metadata-only backups to a signed manifest stored in object store.

5) KMS / keys
- Integrate with customer HSM for key wrapping; store data encryption keys (DEKs) per-blockstore and rotate quarterly.
- We can validate with a staging key; ensure network routes from storage-nodes to HSM are allowed.

6) Egress and image seeding
- Because they are air-gapped, recommend pre-seeding container images via a bundle (OCI tar) and hosting in an on-prem registry. Provide image digests and allowlist for the proxy.
- Outbound: only to their proxy IPs. We'll provide a minimal set of outbound endpoints (NTP, Vault primary, monitoring endpoints) which must be allowed.

Attachments referenced: node-sizing-recommendation.csv (quick per-GPU host profile), redwood-deploy-playbook-snippet.txt

If nobody objects, I'll convert this into 1-slide architecture diagram + 1-page PV lifecycle table for the call.

—PrIyom

Hi Evan — appreciated the sync today. Recap and immediate next steps below (pulled from the meeting and our internal prep):

Recap (decisions / confirmations)- Control plane: 3x control VMs across 2 racks (local etcd raft).
- Node classes: inference-large (8 x A8000 @ 1 GPU/node), inference-medium (6 x nodes with 2x A5000 each), infra (2 nodes), storage (3 nodes for replicated blockstore).
- Storage: ephemeral NVMe on inference nodes for cache; encrypted replicated blockstore for model artifacts; on-prem S3-compatible archive for snapshots.
- KMS: you confirmed vendor is HashiCorp Vault running in a hardened appliance. We'll need network routing to the appliance and a staging key for validation.
- Egress: pre-seeding images + on-prem registry; outbound strictly to your proxy — we've documented the minimal allowlist for required endpoints.

Attachments & artifacts we've shared: node-sizing-recommendation.csv, redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf. Link to the collaborative runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Qstella-deploy-plan

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) Customer: share sustained QPS + model footprints (memory + checkpoints) by 2027-03-24 EOD — this will let us finalize NVMe sizing.
2) Redwood: deliver 1-page architecture diagram, PV lifecycle table, and a short image pre-seeding playbook by 2027-03-26. (PrIyom / Irene are owners).
3) Pilot scope: propose a 2-week pilot (10 GPUs) after artifacts complete; procurement can follow pilot acceptance.

If that matches your expectations, we'll finalize the doc and open a ticket for deployment scheduling.

Thanks all — happy to jump back on a follow-up call if anything changes.

Best,
